html:
In 1931 Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, gave the vote to every adult man and woman over 21. It was the first colony in Asia to adopt universal adult suffrage.

The change came with the Donoughmore Constitution, drawn up after a British commission visited the island in 1927. Before, only a small group of educated, propertied men could vote. The commission argued that power should rest on the whole people. Many in the local elite opposed it as too much, too soon. Women's groups had campaigned for the vote and won it on equal terms with men, only a few years after Britain itself.

The first elections, to a new State Council, were held in 1931.

The reform trained voters and parties for self rule. Ceylon became independent in 1948 with elections already a habit. In 1960 it chose Sirimavo Bandaranaike as the world's first woman prime minister. Mass politics also sharpened rivalry between Sinhalese and Tamils, leading to laws such as the Sinhala Only Act. It compares with women's suffrage in New Zealand.
sum: In 1931 Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, gave the vote to every adult man and woman over 21. It was the first colony in Asia to adopt universal adult suffrage.
